content.text:
No, it isn't fully safe. If you ship `--color-*` and similar names unprefixed, they can collide with variables on your users' sites. The docs say the fix is the `prefix` option.

- **Prefix option:** `@import "tailwindcss" prefix(tw);` prefixes the generated classes and the theme variables. The compiled CSS then has `--tw-color-red-500` and `.tw\:text-red-500` (`src/docs/styling-with-utility-classes.mdx`, "Managing style conflicts → Using the prefix option", lines 992–1020).
- **Keeping `rounded-lg`:** The prefix keeps the built-in utilities. Utilities like `rounded-lg` still work, but they become `tw:rounded-lg` and read the prefixed variables. The docs example shows only color variables, so I haven't confirmed this for radius variables.
- **Unused defaults:** The defaults come from `theme.css`, imported into `@layer theme` (`src/docs/theme.mdx`, "Default theme variables", lines 311–351). I did not read how Tailwind treats unused variables, so I can't say whether they are emitted. I also didn't read the "Using a custom theme" section (`theme.mdx` lines 426–450), which covers resetting a namespace to `initial`.

- **Keeping `rounded-lg`:** The prefix keeps the built-in utilities. Utilities like `rounded-lg` still work, but they become `tw:rounded-lg` and read the prefixed variables. The docs example shows only color variables, so I haven't confirmed this for radius variables.
- **Unused defaults:** The defaults come from `theme.css`, imported into `@layer theme` (`src/docs/theme.mdx`, "Default theme variables", lines 311–351). I did not read how Tailwind treats unused variables, so I can't say whether they are emitted.
